banner.title: The Dragon small variants - the combined issue-1 round: Gold's Languages doctrine (folios 9-10), Smith's Eldar variants (folio 30), and the Bulette lore pin (folio 19)
banner.provenance: Pinned from The Dragon Vol. 1 No. 1 (June 1976): folios 9-10, Lee Gold's Languages; folio 30, Larry Smith's The Three Kindreds of the Eldar; folio 19, Creature Features - the Bulette, the original Landshark appearance, pinned as LORE against the existing MM2 def monsters/monsters/b/bulette.lua, never a competing def. The voice rides extract/dragon/001/. OD&D-era ink converted per the walk doctrine: the pin IS the conversion, noted, never silent.
banner.sentinel: The variant-layer doctrine holds: Dragon ink is never core 1e canon. The Bulette pins are lore/provenance only - the MM2 def itself is untouched and holds the stem; the Eldar multipliers ride as the 150-percent 1e conversion of x1.5; the language doctrine is Gold's prose with its one printed number and its anecdote-grade example.

audit_comment: THE DRAGON SMALL VARIANTS - the combined issue-1 round, three chains on the variant layer. LANGUAGES (Gold, folios 9-10): the 20-percent Common doctrine, the personal-tongue rules (a native tongue beside Common, thinking in it), and mutual comprehensibility by percentage - the Cavish/Morloch 60-percent encounter is the anecdote-grade example. ELDER (Smith, folio 30): the Noldor elf rides no level restriction, all spell ranges and effects at x1.5 (pinned as the 150-percent 1e conversion), and the Blackmoor-borne doctrine that all elves are immune to any and all sickness and disease - variants against the engine's 1e elf canon (races.h, elf.lua), never core rewrites. THE BULETTE (folio 19): the original Landshark appearance, pinned as LORE and PROVENANCE against the existing MM2 def monsters/monsters/b/bulette.lua - the def is untouched, the stem holds, no competing def ever: the two semi-vulnerable spots (the eyes AC 4, the raised-crest underside AC 6), the never-underground doctrine, the six-die smallest, the scales-as-shields and pairs-territorial lore. HONEST BOUNDARIES: all three chains are OD&D-era variant ink, converted, noted, never silent; Gold's doctrine is prose with one printed number; the Eldar multipliers are the only numeric conversions; the Bulette pins never touch the def's own fields. The Ives gap box flips this round - the dragon report's first flip.
